rule.title: Strict Contextual Framing and Anti-Hallucination Prompting
rule.statement: System instructions must explicitly instruct the LLM to answer strictly using the provided context, and to state clearly that information is missing if the context is insufficient.
rule.rationale: Without strict negative constraints, LLMs default to parametric web knowledge, hallucinating plausible but incorrect organizational facts.
rule.implementation_guidance: Include: 'You must answer exclusively using the provided context. If the answer cannot be found, reply: I do not have enough information.'

forbidden.example: System: 'You are a helpful assistant, answer any questions.'

preferred.example: System: 'Rely solely on the facts provided below. Do not assume or extrapolate beyond this text.'

source.evidence_quote: Prompt framing must establish strict epistemic boundaries: the model must be explicitly forbidden from drawing on outside knowledge when answering document queries.

rule.title: Asynchronous Background Processing for Multi-Page Document Ingestion
rule.statement: Documents exceeding 5MB or 20 pages must be ingested asynchronously via background worker jobs, returning an immediate 202 Accepted status with a job status tracking endpoint.
rule.rationale: Synchronous parsing and embedding of a 100-page PDF takes 30-90 seconds, causing HTTP reverse-proxy timeouts (504 Gateway Timeout) and blocking Node.js event loop threads.
rule.implementation_guidance: Accept upload, save file to disk/S3, enqueue BullMQ / background job, return { documentId, status: 'processing' }. Update status via WebSocket or polling.

forbidden.example: Holding the HTTP POST request open for 60 seconds while Mammoth/pdf-parse and Gemini generate 200 embeddings synchronously.

preferred.example: POST /api/v1/documents returns 202 with { jobId: '123', statusUrl: '/api/v1/jobs/123' }; client polls or listens to WS.

source.evidence_quote: Large document ingestion must be decoupled from the synchronous HTTP request-response cycle. Use background workers to extract, chunk, and embed documents asynchronously.

rule.title: Automated Groundedness and Faithfulness Evaluation
rule.statement: RAG generation quality must be continuously audited against a golden evaluation dataset measuring Faithfulness (answer grounded in context) and Answer Relevance.
rule.rationale: Prompt tweaks or model upgrades can silently degrade answer faithfulness or introduce subtle hallucinations without unit test failure.
rule.implementation_guidance: Run an automated evaluation suite comparing model answers against context chunks to compute a Faithfulness Score >= 0.85.

forbidden.example: Relying purely on manual inspection of 2 sample queries when upgrading embedding models.

preferred.example: Automated CI step checking 50 benchmark queries with RAGAS or LLM-as-a-judge for faithfulness.

source.evidence_quote: Evaluating a RAG application requires measuring the RAG triad: context relevance, groundedness (faithfulness), and answer relevance against curated ground truth.
